Sycophancy.d: An AI model's tendency to agree with the user or tell them what they seem to want to hear, even when it isn't true. Partly caused by training on human preference ratings.

Grounding.d: Giving a model the source material (documents, logs, data) and asking it to answer only from that material, so its answer can be checked against the source.

Chunking.d: Splitting documents into smaller passages (chunks) before embedding them, so that search can find and return just the relevant part.

Vector database.d: A database built to store embeddings (vectors) with their text and metadata, and to find the stored vectors nearest to a query vector quickly.

Keyword search.d: Search that matches the exact words in the query, usually scored with a formula such as BM25. Strong for identifiers like ticket numbers; weak on synonyms.

Semantic search.d: Search by meaning rather than exact words: the query and documents are turned into embeddings and the closest ones are returned.

Hybrid search.d: Running keyword search and semantic search together and merging their results, for example with reciprocal rank fusion.

BM25.d: A classic keyword-search scoring formula that rewards rare query words, repeated matches (with diminishing returns) and shorter passages.

Reranking.d: A second retrieval step in which a slower, more accurate model rescores the candidate passages against the query and keeps only the best ones.

Data contamination.d: When benchmark questions or their answers were in a model's training data, so a high score may reflect memory rather than ability.

Benchmark saturation.d: The point at which top models score near the maximum on a benchmark, so it can no longer tell them apart.

Leaderboard.d: A public ranking of AI models by their scores on one or more benchmarks or by human-preference votes.

Elo rating.d: A rating system from chess, used by some AI leaderboards: models gain more points for beating strong opponents than weak ones in head-to-head comparisons.

pass@k.d: A scoring rule that counts a task as solved if any of k attempts succeeds. pass@1 counts only the first attempt and is closest to real use.

Confidence interval.d: A range of values that a true score plausibly lies in, given the size of the test. Overlapping intervals mean a difference may be noise.
